reason: Strong Shorts demand that small channels break into (24 of 29 had a 5x hit), and animated maps suit our flat kit; long videos only win for big channels.
conditions: Build a map component first: country outlines from Natural Earth (public domain), drawn and animated on the flat kit
Disputed borders (Kashmir, Arunachal, Crimea, Taiwan…) follow the official map of the country a video is about, or are left out; facts sourced like channel #1's
Shorts only at launch; long videos only once a Short passes 100K views
The full research drops the off-niche channels the searches pulled in (gangster stories, animal facts, exam prep)
for: 24 of 29 small channels (under 10K subscribers) had a Short at 5x their median or more in 6 months
On-niche Shorts: median 20K views in 90 days, 14% of them hits
The hits are animated maps and 'what if' questions: 'Why Chile is so long and narrow' 10.6M on a 14K channel, 'Can countries roll down a hill' 2.7M on a 3K channel
against: Long videos: median 414K views but from big channels; only 1 small channel had a long hit
Crowded: 42 of 45 channels posted in the last 30 days
Geopolitics touches disputed borders and wars: a wrong map can be illegal (India) or demonetised

earnings.assumptions: Estimates, not sourced figures: 2 Shorts a day; Shorts RPM about $0.03-0.06 per 1,000 views (education/geography); the partner programme by the 10M-Shorts-views-in-90-days path around month 4-8 if one Short breaks out; no long videos in the first 6 months

doable.look: yes, with a new map component (Natural Earth outlines, public domain); the hits are animated maps, flags and simple characters, no footage or faces
doable.voice: yes: English, Kokoro US or UK narrator
doable.policy: care: disputed borders and wars; no AI-content label needed for maps and drawings
